quote: Let X1, X2 be a pair of independent random variables such that Xi ~ EG2(thetai, phi, alphai), i = 1, 2. Furthermore, let X1*, X2* be an another pair of independent random variables with Xi* ~ EG2(thetai*, phi, alphai*), i = 1, 2. Set [alpha1 alpha2; theta1 theta2] = [0.54 0.66; 1.7 1.4] and [alpha*1 alpha*2; theta*1 theta*2] = [0.5 0.7; 1.8 1.3]. We can see that both the matrices belong in S2. Consider a T-transform matrix: T0.8 = 0.8 I + 0.2 Pi = [0.8 0.2; 0.2 0.8], and we have [alpha1 alpha2; theta1 theta2] = [alpha*1 alpha*2; theta*1 theta*2] T0.8, which satisfies the Definition 2.5, so we have [alpha; theta] >> [alpha*; theta*]. Therefore, from Theorem 3.1, we get X1:2 <=st X1:2*, for any x > 0.
